study.title: autoTICI: Automatic Brain Tissue Reperfusion Scoring on 2D DSA Images of Acute Ischemic Stroke Patients

imaging.modality_detail: 2D cerebral DSA sequences, pre- and post-EVT, AP and lateral views; frame rates 0.5-4 fps; mostly only subtracted images stored
imaging.territory_detail: Anterior circulation acute ischemic stroke (intracranial ICA or M1 occlusion) before/after endovascular treatment
imaging.frames_per_sequence: variable; acquisitions with fewer than six frames excluded

public_dataset_used.detail: MR CLEAN Registry (multi-center Dutch registry; not described as publicly downloadable)

annotation.annotator_expertise: Phase labels: one experienced clinician, one colleague researcher and the first author; eTICI reference scored by independent core-lab neuroradiologists

task.task_description: Fully automatic quantitative TICI (reperfusion) scoring: CNN-based DSA phase classification (non-contrast/arterial/parenchymal/venous) with a handcrafted state-transition constraint, affine motion correction, MINIP computation, Frangi/Otsu vessel and perfusion segmentation, atlas-based brain masking, and ratio of reperfused pixels post- vs pre-EVT; evaluated against eTICI and for mRS/NIHSS outcome prediction.
task.clinical_application: Peri-procedural assessment of reperfusion after endovascular treatment of acute ischemic stroke

architecture_names: affine registration (SimpleElastix, Mattes mutual information, ASGD)

temporal_evidence.quote: the input is set to three consecutive 2D sequence frames, each for one input channel. In such a way, local features of three consecutive frames are fused.

method.pretraining: Described as a 'retrained ResNet18'; source of pretrained weights not stated
method.explainability_method: Step-by-step pipeline with intermediate visualizable outputs (phase labels, MINIP, segmentation colormap); no saliency method

metrics.metric: First arterial border frame match accuracy
Last arterial (arterial/parenchymal) border frame match accuracy
Spearman rho autoTICI (AP view) vs eTICI
Spearman rho autoTICI (lateral view) vs eTICI
Micro-average AUC, AP autoTICI predicting eTICI (LOOCV multinomial logistic regression)
Micro-average AUC, lateral autoTICI predicting eTICI (LOOCV multinomial logistic regression)
Micro-average AUC, AP+lateral autoTICI predicting eTICI
AUC for dichotomized mRS (cross-validated logistic regression)
Spearman rho autoTICI vs NIHSS shift

comparators: ablated variants (no augmentation, no temporal neighbors, no transition matrix)
Schuldhaus et al. perceptron-based phase classification (literature numbers)

code_available.detail: Only the elastix registration parameter file is linked (https://elastix.lumc.nl/modelzoo/par0063/)

G1.quote: A pure numerical comparison seems to show comparable performance, but our study has different characteristics.

G2.quote: Due to the large variety in acquisition systems and imaging protocols in different centers as well as differences in patient condition, the acquired DSA images possess great variability in image appearance and quality.

G3.quote: Although 2D CNNs have been shown powerful in extracting representative features from images, temporal information is discarded when handling videos.

G4.quote: As our DSA images are 2D projections of the brain, affine transformations are unable to fix 3D rotation artifacts in its 2D projects.

G5.quote: deep learning based segmentation methods, such as U-Net [47], which is not studied in this work due to the massive amount of annotations required.

G7.quote: end-to-end training approaches generally sacrifices causal interpretability. The proposed method, by contrast, provides intermediate visualizable outputs per step, offering enriched clinical insights

G9.quote: Whereas the distribution of patients with respect to eTICI and mRS is imbalanced, we did not attempt to balance the distribution during data selection

G11.quote: automatic periprocedural imaging biomarker extraction from DSA is yet to be further explored.

other_limitations: Original unsubtracted images mostly discarded in registry; motion correction cannot handle subtraction artefacts
Heavy data exclusion: only 141 of 1488 patients suitable for autoTICI quantification
autoTICI and eTICI definitions not fully identical, so perfect correlation is unattainable
Inter-acquisition variation in contrast dilution and injection volume
Atlas-to-patient registration relies on skull outline and vasculature due to lacking background texture
future_work: Deep learning based perfusion segmentation (e.g., U-Net)
Use original non-subtracted images to improve registration robustness
Fixed injection protocols with mechanical pumps to reduce inter-acquisition variation
Apply phase classification to key frame selection, temporal synchronization and slow arterial flow detection
End-to-end deep learning alternatives for TICI scoring
